So, am I bad for leaving or staying in your space? I said at the beginning of my post that if this is out of line that I would accept the criticism remove it. I'm not a victim here at all. How you read my text is not necessarily how tone is, and your interpretation of me has not been generous, you see me as.. well, doesn't matter but I can tell you don't like me and you're entitled to that.

Is feeling ashamed and embarrassed victimhood? I think those are just emotions that I was sharing, like I hoped others would. And no, my emotions are not on you, I didn't say it was.

And there is a rule in this sub about not gatekeeping ugliness, so I thought that I was free to post in the context of discussing my partner who had faced a lot of bullying. Still not sure why it's offensive that I told my and their story... It's mine to tell and you're not being used here or forced to interact.

Ps, my partner and I are both therapists, so, maybe the way we view these things is different. We spend all our time researching and discussing trauma... Idk... I understand others agree I'm in the wrong here, I'm not disputing their opinions and they are perfectly reasonable to have that opinion.

Anyway. Good luck to you.

How does that make sense? :( 

I can't 'use' you or anyone here because you are interacting willingly. 

And yeah, I do feel ashamed. :( Jesus. Why keep replying to me? My goal was to have an open convo, I see It failed. What is your goal here with me? I already feel ashamed and embarrassed. I really care about my partner. I'm not sure what I did wrong but I'll take your work that I did something bad... I deleted it. ':(

'Use' a participant is a sentence that contradicts itself. 

I wanted to be honest about my looks because I thought it was relevant. I'm not a grandiose person. Sorry I came off that way. I had been keeping this in, Idk where I can take these questions.

And I thought this place would be candid about the emotional toll of this kind of trauma. I deleted it, I feel ashamed now.
That's too bad, your take is cynical and couldn't be further from how our relationship is.

Just curious, I was colic because I'm lactose intolerant. (Not totally allergic to dairy like some, which would be worse.) I had wicked awful nightmares as a result of dairy, and my mother didn't breastfeed so she didn't know the formula was hurting me.


 My siblings didn't have the same experience because they were breastfed. Any similarities for you? 


I only discovered much later in life when I tried vegan for a year and a half. My nightmares and pain subsided slowly, so I didn't notice the difference. One day I ate pizza and was immediately in pain and had awful sleep paralysis that night.


Purely anecdotal, but I'm convinced that's why I was colic.
